page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture instance within the e2 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance exhibits lower-tier compute performance. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with the PassMark CPU score, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the bottom 10%. However, memory performance is relatively stronger, with the PassMark memory score reaching the middle 50% average tier, though uncached large-block memory read and write speeds remain in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with modest compute capabilities, the e2-highmem-4 is structured for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. It is suitable for small-scale database operations, caching layers, and lightweight memory-intensive applications. The instance offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-heavy requirements by avoiding the higher costs associated with faster compute-optimized processors, though it is not suited for high-throughput web serving or intensive data compilation.
